sections.html:
Camillus is a town in Onondaga County, west of Syracuse. The village of Camillus sits in the southwestern part of the town. Before you sell, find out which side of that line your house is on. Village residents deal with two sets of local rules and two tax bills, and that changes who your closing attorney needs to call.

Three routes are open to a Camillus owner: list with an agent, sell privately, or take an offer straight from a company such as ours. About four in five households here own their home, so most sellers are ordinary homeowners rather than investors.

Camillus had an estimated 25,088 people in mid-2025, down 1.0% from the April 2020 base. Staying put is the norm here: 92.2% of residents had the same address a year earlier. The median owned home is valued at $209,000 and the median household income is $85,915, which describes a middle-income suburb. Roughly 21.8% of residents are 65 or older, which means a share of sellers are closing out an estate or leaving a house that has become too big.

Much of the housing dates from the growth years of the 1950s through the 1970s, when the population went from 6,735 to 26,841. Expect an older-house buyer to ask about roof age, heating and electrical.

Camillus has no single downtown. It is a mix of hamlets and subdivisions, and a few of them anchor the housing market.

  • Hamlets: Amboy, Bennetts Corners, Fairmount, Newport, Warners, Memphis and North Belle Isle
  • Neighborhoods near the village: Fox Chapel, Weatheridge, Pioneer Farms, Westview Manor and West Genesee Terrace
  • Southern edge: Scenic Hills, Parson Farms, Stanley Manor and Sherwood Knolls

The town reaches several ZIP codes, including Camillus (13031), Elbridge, Marcellus, Memphis, Warners and parts of Syracuse. Your mailing address may not say Camillus even when the parcel is inside the town. Check the deed and the tax bill rather than the postal city when you fill out listing or closing paperwork.

sections.h2: Selling a Camillus house as it is
sections.html:
An as-is sale lets you leave the paint, the patching and the old carpet alone. You still owe the buyer honest answers about the property, and the closing attorney handles the contract and the deed.

A move-in-ready house competes well against finished homes on the market. A house with a dated kitchen or deferred maintenance does not, and buyers who use a mortgage will ask for repairs or a lower price after the inspection. A direct cash buyer folds the needed work into the price. Gone are the repair haggling, the open houses and the weeks of waiting on a lender, and you choose the closing date.

Jot down what you know about the house before anyone walks through: how old the roof and furnace are, whether the basement ever gets wet, and any work done without a permit. Telling a direct buyer up front speeds the offer, because the price is set once and does not get renegotiated after an inspection.

Commute time is one selling point that holds up: workers here average 21.3 minutes to their jobs, with Syracuse close by. Mention it however you sell.

sections.h2: Recording a deed in Onondaga County
sections.html:
Your Camillus deed is filed with the Onondaga County Clerk. Typical charges on a house sale:

  • $45.50 base fee for a deed, plus $5.00 for each page and $0.50 for each additional surname or cross reference
  • $5.00 to file the TP-584 return, plus $2.00 of state transfer tax for each $500 of price
  • $125.00 for the RP-5217 real property transfer report on an improved residential property
  • $10.00 residential deed note to grantors, required by state law since March 2020

The deed department answers recording questions at 315-435-8250. The closing attorney normally files the papers and collects these amounts, and you can ask to see the totals on the settlement statement before the closing date. In a cash sale the same documents are filed, but there is no lender adding its own recording steps.

Camillus is outside the city of Syracuse, so its bills go through the county's tax services office on the 15th floor of the Civic Center on Montgomery Street. Owners can look up bills, print receipts and pay online.

Two dates matter for late accounts. County taxes unpaid after March 31 and school or village taxes unpaid after November 1 go to that office. It takes calls at 315-435-2426 and accepts mailed checks payable to the Chief Fiscal Officer at PO Box 1004, Syracuse, NY 13201. The county also holds an online tax auction each October, with properties listed from September.

Behind on a bill? Request the exact payoff in writing from the Onondaga County tax office before agreeing to a sale. Whatever you owe comes out of the sale money on closing day, and a surprise balance is a common reason a closing slips. A cash sale can still close quickly if the number is known up front. County exemption applications for parcels outside Syracuse are due March 1, and the town assessor can explain the filing if you plan to list in winter.

sections.h2: Check with the town before you sell
sections.html:
Open the town conversation early, because answers can take a few days. Ask Town of Camillus code enforcement whether any permit on your house was left open, whether a rental on the property needs registration or inspection, and which zoning district applies. An unfinished deck, a basement finished without a permit or an old shed can all surface when a buyer's attorney orders a municipal search.

Town staff can usually confirm the zoning district, the lot lines and whether the house has public sewer or a septic tank. Buyers' attorneys ask about all three.

The signing appointment runs about an hour in most cases. You sign the deed and the transfer forms, the payoff of any loan or tax bill is handled by the attorney from your proceeds, and the balance is paid to you. Nobody is waiting on a bank appraisal when the buyer pays cash.

If the property is in the village, ask the village clerk separately for any village charges. Village taxes have their own November 1 cutoff, so a closing attorney will want both bills in hand.

For your first attorney meeting, gather the deed, the latest school and county tax bills, any village bill, permits and certificates of occupancy for past work, and the mortgage payoff statement if there is a loan.

faqs.q: Is Camillus a town or a village?
faqs.a: Both exist. The Town of Camillus lies west of Syracuse in Onondaga County, and the village of Camillus occupies the southwestern part of it. Your tax bill shows which one levies on your house, and the village clerk can answer questions about village charges.

faqs.q: What is the state transfer tax on a Camillus sale?
faqs.a: The state transfer tax is $2.00 for each $500 of price, reported on the TP-584 return, which carries a $5.00 filing fee. Your closing attorney will total it for your sale.

faqs.q: Which office records my deed after I sell in Camillus?
faqs.a: The Onondaga County Clerk. Recording starts at $45.50 plus $5.00 a page, and the RP-5217 report adds $125.00 on improved residential property.

faqs.q: Can unpaid taxes put a Camillus house in an auction?
faqs.a: They can. The county holds an online tax auction every October, and late taxes outside Syracuse are paid at its tax services office. Paying the balance before you list means nothing is deducted from your proceeds later.

faqs.q: Why does my Camillus house have a Syracuse or Marcellus mailing address?
faqs.a: The town spans several postal areas, including 13031 for Camillus plus Elbridge, Marcellus, Memphis, Warners and Syracuse ZIP codes. The deed and the assessment roll show the legal location.
